translations: Wu Gang carefully counted the wood shavings on the ground and watched as they scattered away, finally confirming that it wasn't just his imagination or a particularly hard spot on the tree trunk that was causing the problem.

As the moonlight filtered through the tree's branches, Wu Gang saw that not a single leaf was missing. He picked up his axe again, this time without boasting to Aman that he was sure to succeed. Instead, he carefully sharpened the blade, looking for a new approach.

Aman put away the green bamboo slips, leaving a note that said the cypress tree would grow back as soon as it was chopped down. Wu Gang's first attempt at brute force had failed, and the real challenge was only just beginning. Every time he made progress, he would have to start all over again, facing the same tree that seemed to mock him with its speed of recovery.
Wu Gang tried to concentrate all his strength in one spot.

He no longer hacked wildly in all directions, but instead aimed each blow at the existing marks on the tree. The tree trunk was cut deep, but it would recover just as quickly as long as there was a brief moment between each blow for the moonlight to seal the edges.

The direct result of brute force was not that the tree fell, but that Wu Gang struggled to hold onto the axe. As the axe began to slip, he would stop just in time to avoid getting hurt. In the past, he would have blamed his exhaustion on the need for more powerful magic; this time, he acknowledged that relying solely on strength wouldn't be enough to keep up with the tree's recovery.

His second approach was to try and chop faster. Wu Gang reduced the swing of his axe, hoping to create a continuous sound. His speed did increase, but the marks became shallower and shallower, and the tree would simply erase them with a single flash of light.

Seeing the result, Wu Gang stopped swinging his axe in frustration. Chopping quickly but inaccurately was like trying to learn multiple skills at once – it looked busy, but he wasn't making any real progress in any one area.

His third approach was to try a different angle. He thought that if he could chop the tree from different sides, the roots or high branches might be more vulnerable. So, he cleared away the moon soil and chopped at the exposed roots. The marks on the roots would also recover, and the moon soil would return to its original place under the tree's light.

He climbed up to a lower branch. The swaying of the branch made it harder to steady the axe, and even if he managed to leave a mark, the cypress leaf would respond by restoring the wood to its original state. Wu Gang didn't dare climb any higher, as failure at that height would only increase the risk of falling.

Each of the three approaches had given him different results: brute force couldn't be sustained, chopping quickly lost its depth, and trying a different angle still didn't work. Wu Gang inscribed the results on the stone next to the tree, no longer lumping all his failures together under the phrase "I still haven't chopped it down today."

There was no other tool in the moon palace for him to try, and the axe had no hidden powers. As Wu Gang sharpened the axe, he suddenly realized that he was still expecting some secret mechanism to reveal itself. Recognizing this thought, he didn't go searching for symbols on the tree, but instead returned to his original spot.

He began to chop the cypress tree at a steady pace. The tree still recovered, and the progress still disappeared, but Wu Gang no longer lost his grip on the axe due to frustration. He could also stop to maintain the axe before his strength gave out, rather than wasting time repairing the damage.

This still didn't create any permanent marks on the tree. The hardest part of the punishment was that the external results remained the same as if nothing had happened. But Wu Gang's actions were no longer focused on "how to leave the moon palace quickly," but on "how to make each axe blow complete."

The night remained unchanged, and the scent of the cypress flowers remained the same. Wu Gang swung his axe, stopped, sharpened, and swung again, repeating the same actions; the only difference was that he no longer mindlessly added force, but instead carefully examined the differences he had previously overlooked.

During his breaks, he thought about the two batches of materials he had ruined. His fellow apprentices, when faced with the same challenge, had no shortcuts to use and had to start over from scratch, searching for new materials. He had then said a hasty apology and tried to move on, but the cypress tree was now teaching him that starting over wouldn't be any easier.

Wu Gang finally acknowledged that all the skill-based approaches would not be able to stop the cypress tree from recovering. If there was a way out of the punishment, it wouldn't be through finding a new, faster method.

He gripped the axe handle and looked at the smooth tree trunk. The next stage was no longer about finding a way to chop the tree, but about why he was so afraid of the endless persistence without seeing a clear end, and whether he could still take responsibility for his mistakes without any tangible results.
It was hard to tell how many days had passed in the moon palace.

The cypress flowers bloomed and fell, only to return to the branches under the moonlight. Wu Gang's axe blows echoed into the human world, where people occasionally caught a glimpse of someone chopping a tree in the moonlight, unaware that each axe mark had been erased countless times.
Wu Gang initially resented the celestial master for setting him an impossible task. He thought he had apologized and was still chopping away, so why couldn't he see any clear progress?

But when he thought about the two batches of materials he had ruined, the answer wasn't so simple. His fellow apprentices didn't know whether they would succeed in the end, but they still waited for the seasons to pass; he had abandoned his post and hurried the process, reducing all their efforts to zero, simply because he couldn't see the quick results.
Each time the cypress tree recovered, it was like being brought back to that moment again.
